title: Nightingale Therapeutics - Renewal & EU Onramp Check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal/expansion check-in. Customer confirmed intent to renew with a 30% capacity uplift and to pilot EU region private onboarding (VPC + KMS). Discussed latency SLOs, data residency, SOC2 evidence, and pricing options for burst vs reserved capacity. Agreed to run a 2-week latency and throughput benchmark in EU, Redwood to send updated SOW and security pack, procurement to review commercial terms. Next technical deep-dive scheduled for 2025-04-22.
topics: EU private onboarding (VPC, KMS, audit logs)
Contract extension options and pricing (reserved vs burst)
action_items: Olivia Ramos - Send updated SOW and redwood security pack (SOC2 report, data flow diagram) - due 2025-04-17
Marcus Li - Schedule EU benchmark window and provide throughput/latency test plan - due 2025-04-18
Dr. Priya Shah - Provide sample production prompt set and expected qps distribution for benchmarking - due 2025-04-17
Sophie Leung - Confirm procurement timeline and preferred commercial terms (monthly vs annual) - due 2025-04-21
next_steps: Redwood to send pricing options (reserved + burst) and draft amendment for 12-month extension
Run 2-week EU private region benchmark (start window: 2025-04-20)
Technical deep-dive on model routing and failover on 2025-04-22
Procurement to review SOW and security artifacts after receipt
transcript:
[00:00] Olivia: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're about 45 minutes on the calendar. Quick intros?
[00:07] Priya: Hi, Priya Shah from Nightingale — Head of ML.
[00:10] Marcus G: Marcus Greene, CTO.
[00:13] Sophie: Sophie Leung, procurement.
[00:15] Olivia: Great. Marcus Li from Redwood, SE, can you say hi real quick?
[00:18] Marcus L: Yeah, hey all, Marcus Li, engineering.
[00:20] Olivia: Cool. Purpose for today: renewal + uplift discussion, and walk through EU onramp ask — VPC/KMS stuff. We want to confirm scope and next steps.
[00:33] Priya: Quick context: production usage has been stable; we're hitting about 380 qps at peak now, forecasting to 500 qps avg over next quarter with new feature flags. So capacity uplift. Also need EU region for data residency, and legal wants private deployment details.
[00:47] Olivia: Got it. Can you remind us the breakdown — embeddings vs generation?
[00:51] Priya: Yeah, roughly 60% generation, 30% embeddings, 10% rerank today. Sequence lengths on gen are spiky — a lot of 512-token runs and some long tail to 2k tokens.
[01:02] Marcus L: That token distribution is helpful. For throughput we typically recommend reserved capacity for the baseline and burst for spikes to control unit economics.
[01:09] Marcus G: One of our questions: what does the EU private onboarding look like timeline-wise and what controls we get on keys? We need KMS that integrates with our HSM.
[01:18] Marcus L: For private (VPC) we offer a customer-managed control plane option. KMS: you can bring keys via a supported KMIP/HSM-backed KMS or integrate with major cloud KMS providers. We do a handshake for key rotation policies, and we can store audit logs in your S3 / syslog endpoint.
[01:33] Sophie: When you say audit logs, is that granular enough for our compliance team — per-request logs with token counts?
[01:39] Marcus L: Yes, we provide per-request metadata including model variant, token counts, latency, model id. Full request payloads for requests marked for retention — but by default PII is scrubbed unless you opt-in.
[01:49] Priya: There's sometimes noise in the transcription, uh, sorry, but — on failover, how fast can you route to a different region without changing client config?
[01:58] Marcus L: We can route by policy. So you can set primary=europe-1 private, fallback=hosted-us or alternate model variant. The client uses the same endpoint, Redwood handles the routing. Failover is typically sub-second for DNS-level and a few seconds for connection re-establishment — but for session-level continuity with long KV cache we recommend model-variant-compatible fallbacks.
[02:20] Olivia: On the contract side — Sophie, are you thinking annual commit or month-to-month?
[02:24] Sophie: Procurement would prefer annual if price is favorable, but our legal needs the renewal amendment to include data residency clauses and SLAs around latency.
[02:33] Olivia: We can draft an amendment with a 12-month extension and a 30% capacity uplift on top of current committed baseline. We'll include an SLA appendix for p99 latency targets.
[02:42] Marcus G: What are realistic p95/p99 numbers in EU for the model family we run?
[02:47] Marcus L: For the quantized family you're using, in our EU private region p95 is around 60–80ms per token under steady-state for short sequences; p99 can be 200–400ms on bursty long token tails. We'll send benchmark numbers and represent them in the SLOs with a fallback policy.
[03:06] Priya: That p99 seems a little wide, cuz for product we need more consistent performance for front-line features. Can you narrow via prioritization?
[03:13] Marcus L: Yes — options: dedicated GPU pool for your tenant (removes noisy neighbor), reserved capacity with guaranteed slots, or aggressive KV/prefix caching on the model side to shave latency on repeated prefixes. Each has cost tradeoffs.
[03:26] Olivia: I'll include three price tiers: standard reserved, reserved+dedicated pool, and reserved+burst.
[03:33] Sophie: Also need SOC2 evidence and SAML SSO flow for our engineers.
[03:37] Marcus L: We'll attach SOC2 Type II report and a SAML integration guide. For SSO we support SAML and OIDC, and RBAC can be tied to your identity provider groups.
[03:47] Priya: For benchmarking — we'd like to run a realistic prompt set; we'll provide prompt corpus and expected qps.
[03:52] Olivia: Great — action: Priya send prompt set and qps distribution. Marcus Li will propose test windows. We'll do a two-week window in EU starting week of 20th.
[04:03] Marcus G: Can Redwood run a certification test that proves no data leaves EU region when private onramp is used?
[04:08] Marcus L: Yes, we can show the routing topology, VPC peering maps, NAT configs, and we can provide a signed attestation and packet flow diagrams. For absolute air-gap we support on-prem package but that's heavier.
[04:21] Sophie: Pricing question — if we go reserved 30% uplift, is the uplift linear or do you offer step discounts?
[04:27] Olivia: We typically provide step discounts at committed tiers — your uplift size would land you in tier 2, which reduces per-token unit by ~12% vs current. Annual commitment yields an additional 6% discount.
[04:36] Sophie: Okay. We'll review that with finance.
[04:38] Priya: One more on tooling: will we get token-level cost breakdowns per route for the EU cluster? We need that to attribute engineering cost centers.
[04:45] Marcus L: Yes — Redwood Console surfaces token-level cost per model and route, and you can filter by project/team tags. We'll enable export to your billing S3 bucket.
[04:55] Marcus G: Any potential blockers from Redwood side for integrating our HSM?
[04:59] Marcus L: Generally no, as long as your HSM supports standard KMIP or we can do a cloud-KMS proxy. We'll need a short security questionnaire and to schedule a key-handover call.
[05:09] Olivia: Alright let's recap and put owners. Olivia to send SOW and pricing by Thursday. Marcus L to schedule EU benchmark and share test plan. Priya to send prompt corpus. Sophie to confirm procurement timeline. We tentatively set technical deep-dive 2025-04-22.
[05:24] Priya: Sounds good.
[05:26] Sophie: One last question — competitor benchmarking. Marcus G: We did a quick eval of CloudServe AI and Apex and found Redwood had better steady-state costs for our workload but CloudServe's claimed geo-SLA was slightly better.
[05:38] Marcus L: We can provide a cost-run simulation for your exact qps and prompt mix to compare reserved vs alternatives.
[05:45] Olivia: Cool. Any other items?
[05:48] Priya: No, thanks.
[05:49] Marcus G: No.
[05:50] Olivia: Great, thanks everyone. Will follow up with the artifacts. Bye.
[05:55] (call ends)

Notes about transcript quality: occasional transcription errors — e.g., 'K V cash' for KV cache, 'V P C' spacing; some speaker labels overlap. The technical sections captured concreate commitments and the team agreed to a 2-week EU benchmark followed by SOW and contract amendment.
